task: Fix divide in arithmetic.py: ordinary division should work, and dividing by zero must raise ValueError with the message 'zero divisor'. Preserve the other function. Verify both normal and zero-divisor cases.

Fix cambium.render.render_tokens_per_s so that passing None returns an empty string, as the other render helpers do. Keep normal generation-rate behavior unchanged. Change only src/cambium/render.py. Run direct Python assertions for None and a completion_tokens=20, latency_s=2 usage event. No dependency changes.
check: from cambium.render import render_tokens_per_s as rate; assert rate(None)==''; assert rate([])==''; assert rate([{'kind':'usage_event','payload':{'usage':{'completion_tokens':20,'total_tokens':9999},'latency_s':2}}])=='tokens/s=10.0'

task: Implement slug(text) in textutil.py. Lowercase the text, replace each run of non-ASCII-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen, and trim leading/trailing hyphens. Empty or punctuation-only input returns the empty string. Use the standard library and verify representative cases.
check: from textutil import slug; assert slug(' Hello, WORLD! ')== 'hello-world'; assert slug('a---b')=='a-b'; assert slug('')==''; assert slug('!!!')==''; assert slug('r2 d2')=='r2-d2'

task: Complete the independent arithmetic and text utility modules. In arithmetic.py implement clamp(value, low, high), raising ValueError for low > high, and mean(values), raising ValueError for empty input. In textutil.py implement slug(text), lowercase ASCII letters/digits joined with hyphens for punctuation runs, and words(text), returning case-insensitive whitespace-delimited word counts. Each module is an independent workstream with its own examples; keep ownership separate. Verify each module and the combined result. Change only these two files.

Implement group_pairs(pairs) in grouping.py: consume an iterable of (key,value) pairs and return a dict mapping each key to a list of its values in input order. Preserve repeated values. Empty input returns an empty dict. Verify an iterator as well as a list.
check: from grouping import group_pairs; assert group_pairs(iter([('a',1),('b',2),('a',3),('a',1)]))=={'a':[1,3,1],'b':[2]}; assert group_pairs([])=={}
